frase_gancho.texto: Neptune, Venus and the Danaids are the work of nineteenth-century French sculptors, and today they adorn a park in Mexico City.

puente_narrativo.texto: Continue toward the southern edge of the park, the one facing Juárez Avenue. A marble monument with columns awaits you there.

como_llegar.texto: Follow the paths into the interior of the park. The first fountains appear among the trees, and each one brings its own story.

guion_corto.texto: Look for the Roman god of the sea. It is the Neptune fountain, the work of the French sculptor Dubray and cast by the Val d’Osne foundry. It has stood in the Alameda since eighteen eighty-nine. It is not alone. Along the paths there are fountains with Venus, with Mercury, with the Danaids and with a figure of Spring, several of them by French sculptors. People call the Danaids fountain Las Comadres or Las Aguadoras. There is also a monument to Beethoven, a gift from the German community in nineteen twenty-one. Between one piece and the next, the Alameda becomes an open-air sculpture museum.

guion_largo.texto:
If you stroll through the Alameda without hurrying, you will see that almost every fountain has an author with a first and last name. Several pieces were moved during the remodelings, so you may find them in places different from where you imagine.

Let us begin with Neptune. He is the Roman god of the sea, and this fountain is the work of the French sculptor Dubray. It was cast by the Val d’Osne foundry, a French foundry. It has been in the Alameda since eighteen eighty-nine, which means it has presided over the park for more than a century and a quarter. Notice how the figure dominates the center of the fountain.

The fountain of Venus and the Zephyrs is by the French sculptor Mathurin Moreau. The Danaids fountain, by Albert Carrier-Belleuse, is known among local residents as Las Comadres or Las Aguadoras. The Danaids are figures from Greek mythology: the daughters of King Danaus, condemned in the underworld to fill a broken vessel. That is why they appear carrying water, and why the figure suits a fountain so well. The Zephyrs, for their part, are the gentle winds from the west, and they accompany Venus in her fountain.

The Spring fountain is the work of Louis Sauvageau and shows a woman carrying a pitcher. The Mercury fountain, honoring the messenger of the Roman gods, is inspired by the work of the Renaissance master Giambologna. And the fountain of the Americas, by Hubert Lavigne, shows a woman on a double-basin pedestal, surrounded by circular benches.

There are also monuments of another kind. One is the monument to Beethoven, a gift from the German community in nineteen twenty-one. Another is a replica of Malgré tout, which in French means in spite of everything. It is a work from eighteen ninety-eight by the Mexican sculptor Jesús F. Contreras.

The pieces in this park have had a difficult life. Between nineteen seventy-three and nineteen eighty-three, fountains were repaired, and several marble sculptures were replaced with replicas. In two thousand twelve there was another rehabilitation. For that reason, what you see today is a mixture of originals, restorations and copies, and it is worth paying attention to the details of each one.

All of this has a reason behind it. In the nineteenth century, the park’s viceregal sculptures were replaced by new works, and several were commissioned from France. That is why walking through the Alameda is also a glimpse into the tastes of an era, the era of European fountains in the public gardens of capital cities. And since each piece has its own story, you do not need to see them all. If you stop at just two or three, you will already have seen the essentials.

Soon you will reach the Hemiciclo a Juárez, another marble work of Italian origin, this one from the twentieth century. But first, stay a moment among the fountains and think about how many hands and countries took part in a single park in the capital.

texto: Look for the Neptune fountain, the Roman god of the sea
Find a fountain with a woman on a double-basin pedestal, surrounded by circular benches: it is the fountain of the Americas
Locate the monument to Beethoven and take a look at its pedestal

texto.Location: interior paths of the Alameda Central
texto.Key fact: Neptune has been in the Alameda since 1889

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Venus fountain was a gift from Maximilian and Carlota.
texto.respuesta: Reality: It is said to have been donated in 1886, but Maximilian was executed by firing squad in 1867, so that date cannot be correct. What is certain is that the fountain is the work of the French sculptor Mathurin Moreau.
